title: Should have, could have, must have
goal: Talk about past regrets and guesses
intro: Modal + have + past participle talks about the past. “Should have” is a regret or criticism: it didn’t happen, but it was a good idea. “Could have” is a possibility that didn’t happen. “Must have” is a strong guess about the past. In speech they sound like “shoulda”, “coulda”, “musta”.

rules.rule: should have done = it was a good idea, but it didn’t happen.
could have done = it was possible, but it didn’t happen.
must have done = I’m almost sure it happened.

mistakes.why: Past guess: must have + past participle.
“Should’ve” sounds like “should of”, but the word is “have”.

ex.q: The ground is wet. It ___ at night.
Why did you walk? You ___ a taxi.
You ___ shouted at him. He felt bad.
We should have took the earlier flight.
ex.fixed: We should have taken the earlier flight.

ex.q: She must have forget her phone.
ex.fixed: She must have forgotten her phone.

ex.q: You should had asked me first.
ex.fixed: You should have asked me first.

ex.q: He isn’t answering. He ___ have gone to sleep.

ex.a: I should have saved more money.

ex.q: Say a regret with “should have”: you didn’t bring an umbrella and got wet.
a: I should have brought an umbrella
I should have taken an umbrella
I should have carried an umbrella
ex.y: I should have brought an umbrella.

talk: Talk about a decision you regret and what you should have done instead, and something you could have done but didn’t.
